title: U.S. House · Florida's 15th District
area: West-central Florida, including parts of Hillsborough and Polk counties east of Tampa.

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Laurel Lee advanced unopposed. Robert People won the Democratic primary with 53.7% of the vote against Christopher Irizarry.

candidates.name: Laurel Lee

summary.text: Laurel Lee is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Florida's 15th Congressional District. An attorney and former federal prosecutor and public defender, she previously served as Florida's Secretary of State.

background.text: Earned undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Florida.
Worked as an attorney with Carlton Fields, P.A., an assistant federal public defender, an assistant U.S. attorney for the Middle District of Florida, and a law clerk to Judge James S. Moody.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2022; assumed office in January 2023.

record.text: Assigned to chair the Committee on House Administration's Elections Subcommittee and serve as Vice Chair of the full Committee on House Administration and the Joint Committee on the Library, plus seats on the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on Judiciary, for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Lee has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no additional sourced statements of current priorities or issue positions were found in the time available.

summary.text: Robert People is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 15th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army veteran of 21 years, he is running on protecting Social Security, expanding women's reproductive and health rights, and raising teacher pay.

background.text: Age 46; retired from the U.S. Army after 21 years of service.
Attended Parkville High School in Baltimore, Maryland.

priorities.text: Protecting Social Security, including a proposal that the government return "full amounts" it has collected to beneficiaries.
Women's reproductive and health rights, including reversing what he calls "harmful policies" on abortion access.
Raising teacher salaries, starting with District 15, by shifting county school-budget funds away from what he calls wasteful spending.

positions.summary: Says he wants to reverse what he calls harmful policies restricting women's reproductive and health rights.
Lists protecting Social Security among his top three campaign priorities.

candidates.name: Angie Boone

summary.text: Angie Boone is a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 15th Congressional District in the November 3, 2026 general election.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia biography page, campaign website, or completed Candidate Connection survey was found for Boone in the time available.
